plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and slender spikes of tiny tubular flowers. It is widely cultivated in gardens and fields and is a magnet for bees and butterflies. Its flowers are harvested for essential oils, culinary use, and sachets.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-June to August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Mediterranean region, southern France (Provence), England, and temperate gardens across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: The name lavender likely comes from the Latin 'lavare' meaning 'to wash', as the Romans used it to scent baths and laundry.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large round leaves held above the water and showy, cup-shaped flowers up to 30 cm across. The leaves repel water thanks to a nanostructured surface. Flowers open in the morning and close by afternoon over several days.
plants.location: Asia (India, China, Japan, Vietnam), northern Australia, and ornamental ponds worldwide
plants.funFact: Lotus flowers can regulate their own temperature, staying around 30-35°C even when the air is much cooler, and seeds have germinated after more than 1,000 years.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: A hardy North American prairie perennial with daisy-like flowers featuring drooping pinkish-purple petals around a spiky, orange-brown central cone. It thrives in full sun and tolerates drought and poor soils. Goldfinches feed on the seed heads in late summer.
plants.location: Eastern and central United States prairies and open woodlands; widely grown in gardens across temperate regions
plants.funFact: Echinacea comes from the Greek 'echinos' meaning hedgehog, referring to the spiny central cone, and Native American peoples used it medicinally for centuries.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking evergreen shrub with the largest flower heads in the Proteaceae family, reaching up to 30 cm wide. The bloom is made of petal-like bracts surrounding a central cluster of tiny true flowers. It is adapted to fire-prone, nutrient-poor fynbos habitat.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere late winter to spring, with scattered blooms from May to September
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape of South Africa; cultivated in Australia, California, and Hawaii
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower, and the genus is named after the Greek god Proteus because of the many forms the family takes.
